findings.title: canManage() grants group management access when caller only has VIEW permission
findings.body: In GroupPermissionsV2.canManage(), hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE) is called instead of checking only AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE (and the same mistake is documented in GroupPermissionEvaluator.canManage() at line 75). Because GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup() checks auth.groups().requireManage(), any admin granted only the 'view' scope on the all-groups resource will pass requireManage() and be able to create new top-level groups or move existing subgroups to the top level.

findings.title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() fails to find per-group resources and returns Resource IDs instead of Group IDs
findings.body:
GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() is broken in three ways:
1. AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource() (line 121) never calls resource.setType(resourceType) when creating a resource for an individual group; only the 'all-groups' resource created in AdminPermissionsSchema.init() has its type set to AdminPermissionsSchema.GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE. As a result, resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...) never finds any individual group resources.
2. Inside the findByType callback, groupResource.getId() (the internal UUID of the authorization Resource entity) is passed to hasPermission(...) and added to granted, whereas the GroupModel ID is stored in groupResource.getName(). Because hasPermission(String groupId, ...) looks up the resource via resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId), passing groupResource.getId() misses the group resource and falls back to the 'all-groups' resource, and granted.add(groupResource.getId()) collects Resource UUIDs rather than GroupModel IDs.
3. Because the 'all-groups' resource itself has type 'Groups', findByType visits it as well; if an 'all-groups' permission grants view-members or manage-members, its non-group Resource ID is added to granted.

Consequently, for admins with view-members or manage-members on specific groups, getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() always returns an empty set, causing UsersResource.getUsersCount() to return 0 and user searches to skip setting the UserModel.GROUPS session attribute. Conversely, for admins with view-members or manage-members on all groups, UserModel.GROUPS is set to the 'all-groups' Resource UUID, causing user searches to match no group and return 0 users.

findings.title: Javadoc for requireManageMembers references canManageMembership instead of canManageMembers
findings.body: The Javadoc on GroupPermissionEvaluator.requireManageMembers(GroupModel) states 'Throws ForbiddenException if {@link #canManageMembership(GroupModel)} returns {@code false}', but the implementation checks canManageMembers(GroupModel).
